statement: The contractor must establish and maintain an acceptable property management system.
quote: The Contractor shall establish and maintain an acceptable property management system

statement: Failure to maintain an acceptable property management system may result in disapproval of the system by the contracting officer and/or withholding of payments.
quote: Failure to maintain an acceptable property management system, as defined in this clause, may result in disapproval of the system by the Contracting Officer and/or withholding of payments

statement: The contractor's property management system must be in accordance with paragraphs (b) and (f) of the contract clause at Federal Acquisition Regulation 52.245-1.
quote: The Contractor's property management system shall be in accordance with paragraphs (b) and (f) of the contract clause at Federal Acquisition Regulation 52.245-1

statement: The contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the contracting officer that identifies material weaknesses in its property management system.
quote: The Contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the Contracting Officer that identifies material weaknesses in the Contractor's property management system

statement: After the final determination of material weaknesses, the contractor has 45 days from receipt either to correct them or to submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate them.
quote: within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the material weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the material weaknesses

statement: If the contracting officer makes a final determination to disapprove the property management system and the contract includes the Contractor Business Systems clause, payments are withheld in accordance with that clause.
quote: If the Contracting Officer makes a final determination to disapprove the Contractor's property management system, and the contract includes the clause at 252.242-7005, Contractor Business Systems, the Contracting Officer will withhold payments in accordance with that clause

statement: The property management system means the contractor's system or systems for managing and controlling Government property.
quote: Property management system means the Contractor's system or systems for managing and controlling Government property

statement: An acceptable property management system is a property system that complies with the system criteria in paragraph (c) of the clause.
quote: Acceptable property management system means a property system that complies with the system criteria in paragraph (c) of this clause

statement: A material management and accounting system is the contractor's system or systems for planning, controlling and accounting for the acquisition, use, issuing and disposition of material.
quote: Material management and accounting system (MMAS) means the Contractor's system or systems for planning, controlling, and accounting for the acquisition, use, issuing, and disposition of material

statement: An acceptable material management and accounting system is one that generally complies with the system criteria in paragraph (d) of the clause.
quote: Acceptable material management and accounting system means a material management and accounting system that generally complies with the system criteria in paragraph (d) of this clause

statement: The system must ensure that costs of purchased and fabricated material charged or allocated to a contract are based on valid time-phased requirements.
quote: Ensures that costs of purchased and fabricated material charged or allocated to a contract are based on valid time-phased requirements

statement: A 98 percent bill of material accuracy and a 95 percent master production schedule accuracy are desirable as a goal so that requirements are both valid and appropriately time-phased.
quote: A 98 percent bill of material accuracy and a 95 percent master production schedule accuracy are desirable as a goal in order to ensure that requirements are both valid and appropriately time-phased

statement: The system must maintain adequate record accuracy and reconcile recorded inventory quantities to physical inventory by part number periodically, and a 95 percent accuracy level is desirable.
quote: Establish and maintain adequate levels of record accuracy, and include reconciliation of recorded inventory quantities to physical inventory by part number on a periodic basis. A 95 percent accuracy level is desirable

statement: Significant changes in the system must be disclosed to the administrative contracting officer at least 30 days prior to implementation.
quote: Disclose significant changes in its MMAS to the ACO at least 30 days prior to implementation

statement: The procedures for the loan/pay-back technique must be approved by the administrative contracting officer.
quote: The procedures for the loan/pay-back technique must be approved by the ACO

statement: The system should transfer parts and associated costs within the same billing period, except that in the few instances where this is not appropriate the contractor may use the loan/pay-back technique.
quote: The system should transfer parts and associated costs within the same billing period. In the few instances where this may not be appropriate, the Contractor may accomplish the material transaction using a loan/pay-back technique.

statement: The costing methodology may be standard or actual cost, or any of the inventory costing methods in 48 CFR 9904.411-50(b), and the contractor shall maintain consistency across all contract and customer types and from accounting period to accounting period for initial charging and transfer charging.
quote: The costing methodology may be standard or actual cost, or any of the inventory costing methods in 48 CFR 9904.411-50(b). The Contractor shall maintain consistency across all contract and customer types, and from accounting period to accounting period for initial charging and transfer charging.

statement: The contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the contracting officer that identifies material weaknesses in its system.
quote: The Contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the Contracting Officer that identifies material weaknesses in the Contractor's MMAS

statement: After the final determination of material weaknesses, the contractor has 45 days from receipt either to correct them or to submit an acceptable corrective action plan.
quote: the Contractor shall, within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the material weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan

statement: If the contracting officer makes a final determination to disapprove the system and the contract includes the Contractor Business Systems clause, payments are withheld in accordance with that clause.
quote: If the Contracting Officer makes a final determination to disapprove the Contractor's MMAS, and the contract includes the clause at 252.242-7005, Contractor Business Systems, the Contracting Officer will withhold payments in accordance with that clause

statement: On request, the contractor must give the administrative contracting officer the results of the internal reviews it conducted to ensure compliance with its established system policies, procedures and operating instructions.
quote: Provide to the Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO), upon request, the results of internal reviews that it has conducted to ensure compliance with established MMAS policies, procedures, and operating instructions

statement: For this clause, contractor means a business unit as defined in Federal Acquisition Regulation 2.101.
quote: Contractor means a business unit as defined in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 2.101

statement: The contracting officer evaluates the contractor's response and notifies the contractor in writing of the final determination concerning remaining material weaknesses and the adequacy of any proposed or completed corrective action.
quote: The Contracting Officer will evaluate the Contractor's response and notify the Contractor, in writing, of the Contracting Officer's final determination concerning— (i) Remaining material weaknesses; (ii) The adequacy of any proposed or completed corrective action;

statement: The final determination also concerns system disapproval, if the contracting officer determines that one or more material weaknesses remain.
quote: (iii) System disapproval, if the Contracting Officer determines that one or more material weaknesses remain.

statement: If the contractor disagrees with the initial determination, the contractor shall state, in writing, its rationale for disagreeing.
quote: If the Contractor disagrees with the initial determination, the Contractor shall state, in writing, its rationale for disagreeing.

statement: The contracting officer evaluates the contractor's response and notifies the contractor in writing of the final determination concerning remaining material weaknesses and the adequacy of any proposed or completed corrective action.
quote: The Contracting Officer will evaluate the Contractor's response and notify the Contractor, in writing, of the Contracting Officer's final determination concerning— (i) Remaining material weaknesses; (ii) The adequacy of any proposed or completed corrective action;

statement: The final determination also concerns system disapproval, if the contracting officer determines that one or more material weaknesses remain.
quote: (iii) System disapproval if the Contracting Officer determines that one or more material weaknesses remain.

statement: If the contractor disagrees with the initial determination, the contractor shall state, in writing, its rationale for disagreeing.
quote: If the Contractor disagrees with the initial determination, the Contractor shall state, in writing, its rationale for disagreeing.

statement: If systems have bill of material or master production schedule accuracy levels below the stated goals, the contractor shall provide adequate evidence that there is no material harm to the Government due to the lower accuracy levels and that the cost to meet the accuracy goals is excessive in relation to the impact on the Government.
quote: If systems have accuracy levels below these, the Contractor shall provide adequate evidence that— (A) There is no material harm to the Government due to lower accuracy levels; and (B) The cost to meet the accuracy goals is excessive in relation to the impact on the Government;

statement: If a system has a record accuracy level below 95 percent, the contractor shall provide adequate evidence that there is no material harm to the Government due to lower accuracy levels and that the cost to meet the accuracy goal is excessive in relation to the impact on the Government.
quote: If systems have an accuracy level below 95 percent, the Contractor shall provide adequate evidence that— (i) There is no material harm to the Government due to lower accuracy levels; and (ii) The cost to meet the accuracy goal is excessive in relation to the impact on the Government;

statement: Negotiated contracts and subcontracts of $35 million or less are exempt from all CAS requirements; the value is tested at award, using the ceiling for indefinite-delivery contracts and each order under a multiple-award contract.
quote: Negotiated contracts and subcontracts not in excess of $35 million.
note: Was $2.5 million before 2026-10-01; the same rule ended the $7.5 million trigger contract (91 FR 56056, S-0028). 9903.201-1(c) sets how the value is tested.

statement: Full CAS coverage applies to a business unit that receives a single CAS-covered award of $100 million or more, or $100 million or more in net CAS-covered awards in its preceding cost accounting period.
quote: Receive a single CAS-covered contract award of $100 million or more
note: Was $50 million before 2026-10-01 (S-0028); 9903.201-2(b)(4) lets units move to modified coverage.

statement: A business unit selected for a CAS-covered contract or subcontract of $100 million or more must submit a Disclosure Statement before award.
quote: Any business unit that is selected to receive a CAS-covered contract or subcontract of $100 million or more shall submit a Disclosure Statement before award.

statement: When a DoD contracting officer's final determination on material weaknesses in a contractor business system includes a notice to withhold, the contracting officer withholds 5 percent of amounts due from progress and performance-based payments.
quote: the Contracting Officer will withhold 5 percent of amounts due from progress payments and performance-based payments
note: The same paragraph directs the contractor to withhold 5 percent from interim cost vouchers. Total withholds may not exceed 5 percent for one system or 10 percent for several, (e)(3)(i).

statement: The penalty for unallowable costs in final indirect cost rate proposals applies to contracts over $1 million, except the excluded fixed-price types.
quote: This section applies to all contracts in excess of $1 million, except fixed-price contracts without cost incentives or any firm-fixed-price contracts for the purchase of commercial products or commercial services.
note: RFO 42.508-1(b) (S-0019) renumbers it with the same wording; DoD uses it under Class Deviation 2026-O0050.

statement: On a DoD contract, the total business-system withhold from each progress payment, performance-based payment or interim cost voucher may not exceed 10 percent when material weaknesses are in more than one contractor business system.
quote: Ten percent for material weaknesses in multiple contractor business systems
note: The cap for weaknesses in a single system is 5 percent, (e)(3)(i)(A); see CL-CMP-0004.

statement: A cost is allowable only when it complies with all of the following: reasonableness, allocability, standards promulgated by the CAS Board if applicable (otherwise generally accepted accounting principles and practices appropriate to the circumstances), the terms of the contract, and any limitations set forth in FAR subpart 31.2.
quote: A cost is allowable only when the cost complies with all of the following requirements: (1) Reasonableness. (2) Allocability.
note: RFO FAR 31.201-2(a) retains the same allowability requirements.

statement: The contracting officer may disallow all or part of a claimed cost that is inadequately supported by the contractor's records.
quote: The contracting officer may disallow all or part of a claimed cost that is inadequately supported.
note: Renumbered to paragraph (d)(2) in RFO FAR 31.201-2.

statement: A cost is reasonable if, in its nature and amount, it does not exceed that which would be incurred by a prudent person in the conduct of competitive business.
quote: A cost is reasonable if, in its nature and amount, it does not exceed that which would be incurred by a prudent person in the conduct of competitive business.
note: RFO FAR 31.201-3(a) defines reasonableness using reasonable person instead of prudent person.

statement: No presumption of reasonableness attaches to the incurrence of costs by a contractor.
quote: No presumption of reasonableness shall be attached to the incurrence of costs by a contractor.
note: In RFO FAR 31.201-3(a)(1), this rule is set forth in a separate subparagraph.

statement: A cost is allocable if it is assignable or chargeable to one or more cost objectives on the basis of relative benefits received or other equitable relationship.
quote: A cost is allocable if it is assignable or chargeable to one or more cost objectives on the basis of relative benefits received or other equitable relationship.
note: In RFO FAR 31.201-4, this fundamental requirement is designated paragraph (a).

statement: Subject to the general allocability definition (assignable or chargeable to cost objectives on the basis of relative benefits received or other equitable relationship), a cost is allocable to a Government contract if it is necessary to the overall operation of the business, although a direct relationship to any particular cost objective cannot be shown.
quote: Is necessary to the overall operation of the business, although a direct relationship to any particular cost objective cannot be shown.
note: In RFO FAR 31.201-4, this base category is renumbered from paragraph (c) to paragraph (d).

statement: Costs of amusement, diversions, social activities, and directly associated costs are unallowable.
quote: Costs of amusement, diversions, social activities, and any directly associated costs such as tickets to shows or sports events, meals, lodging, rentals, transportation, and gratuities are unallowable.
note: RFO FAR 31.205-14(a) structures the principle into lettered paragraphs and references sporting events.

statement: Costs made specifically unallowable under the entertainment cost principle are not allowable under any other cost principle.
quote: Costs made specifically unallowable under this cost principle are not allowable under any other cost principle.
note: RFO FAR 31.205-14(c) contains the same rule.

statement: Travel costs incurred by contractor personnel on official company business are allowable, subject to the limitations in the travel cost principle.
quote: Costs incurred by contractor personnel on official company business are allowable, subject to the limitations contained in this subsection.
note: RFO FAR 31.205-46(a)(1) contains the same general allowability rule.

statement: Where actual costs above the maximum per diem rates are allowable in special or unusual situations, documentation must follow the contractor's established practices (subject to paragraph (a)(7)), and a receipt is required for each expenditure of $75.00 or more.
quote: a receipt is required for each expenditure of $75.00 or more.
note: RFO FAR 31.205-46(a)(3)(iv) retains the $75 receipt threshold for actual expense method claims.

statement: Airfare costs above the lowest priced airfare available to the contractor during normal business hours are unallowable except when the accommodations require circuitous routing, require travel during unreasonable hours, or excessively prolong travel; the same sentence lists further circumstances, which the next claim quotes.
quote: Airfare costs in excess of the lowest priced airfare available to the contractor during normal business hours are unallowable except when such accommodations require circuitous routing, require travel during unreasonable hours, excessively prolong travel
note: RFO FAR 31.205-46(b) structures the excess airfare restrictions and exceptions under subsection (b)(1).

statement: Except as provided in paragraphs (d) and (e) of FAR 31.205-18 or in agency regulations, costs for IR&D and B&P are allowable as indirect expenses on contracts to the extent that those costs are allocable and reasonable.
quote: costs for IR&D and B&P are allowable as indirect expenses on contracts to the extent that those costs are allocable and reasonable.
note: Under FAR 31.205-18(c), IR&D and B&P costs are allowable as indirect expenses subject to allocability and reasonableness.

statement: Under DFARS 231.205-18(a), a major contractor is any contractor whose covered segments allocated a total of more than $11 million in IR&D and B&P costs to covered contracts during the preceding fiscal year; segments that allocated less than $1,100,000 are not counted toward that total.
quote: Major contractor means any contractor whose covered segments allocated a total of more than $11 million in IR&D costs and B&P costs to covered contracts during the preceding fiscal year.
note: Major contractors are subject to the DTIC reporting and allowability requirements in DFARS 231.205-18(c).

statement: Under DFARS 231.205-18(a), a covered segment is a product division of the contractor that allocated more than $1,100,000 in IR&D and B&P costs to covered contracts during the preceding fiscal year; a contractor with no product divisions is itself the covered segment as a whole.
quote: Covered segment means a product division of the contractor that allocated more than $1,100,000 in independent research and development (IR&D) costs and bid and proposal (B&P) costs to covered contracts during the preceding fiscal year.
note: Segments allocating less than $1,100,000 are not subject to the allowability limitations in DFARS 231.205-18(c).

statement: A contractor's practices used in estimating costs to price a proposal must be consistent with the cost accounting practices used in accumulating and reporting costs.
quote: A contractor's practices used in estimating costs in pricing a proposal shall be consistent with his cost accounting practices used in accumulating and reporting costs.

statement: Practices used in estimating costs in a proposal and in accumulating and reporting costs on the resulting contract must be consistent as to (1) classifying cost elements or functions as direct or indirect, (2) the indirect cost pools to which each element or function is charged or proposed to be charged, and (3) the methods of allocating indirect costs to the contract.
quote: shall be consistent with respect to: (1) The classification of elements or functions of cost as direct or indirect; (2) The indirect cost pools to which each element or function of cost is charged or proposed to be charged; and (3) The methods of allocating indirect costs to the contract.

statement: The grouping of homogeneous costs in estimates prepared for proposal purposes is not per se an inconsistent application of cost accounting practices, subject to the condition stated in the next claim.
quote: The grouping of homogeneous costs in estimates prepared for proposal purposes shall not per se be deemed an inconsistent application of cost accounting practices

statement: All costs incurred for the same purpose in like circumstances are either direct costs only or indirect costs only with respect to final cost objectives.
quote: All costs incurred for the same purpose, in like circumstances, are either direct costs only or indirect costs only with respect to final cost objectives.

statement: A final cost objective cannot receive a cost as an indirect cost if other costs incurred for the same purpose in like circumstances were included as a direct cost.
quote: No final cost objective shall have allocated to it as an indirect cost any cost, if other costs incurred for the same purpose, in like circumstances, have been included as a direct cost of that or any other final cost objective.

statement: A contractor's Disclosure Statement, by distinguishing direct from indirect costs and describing the criteria and circumstances for items sometimes treated as direct and sometimes as indirect, is determinative of whether costs are incurred for the same purpose; if no Disclosure Statement was submitted, the contractor's practices at the time of the proposal are used.
quote: by describing the criteria and circumstances for allocating those items which are sometimes direct and sometimes indirect, will be determinative as to whether or not costs are incurred for the same purpose.

statement: Costs that are expressly unallowable or mutually agreed unallowable must be identified and excluded from any billing, claim, or proposal on a Government contract.
quote: Costs expressly unallowable or mutually agreed to be unallowable, including costs mutually agreed to be unallowable directly associated costs, shall be identified and excluded from any billing, claim, or proposal applicable to a Government contract.

statement: Unallowable costs covered by 9904.405-40(a) through (d) that would normally be part of a regular indirect-cost allocation base remain in that base.
quote: In circumstances where these unallowable costs normally would be part of a regular indirect-cost allocation base or bases, they shall remain in such base or bases.

statement: To provide visibility for incurred unallowable costs, one acceptable practice is to segregate them in separate accounts maintained for that purpose in the regular books of account.
quote: The segregation of unallowable costs in separate accounts maintained for this purpose in the regular books of account

statement: A contractor must use its fiscal year as its cost accounting period, subject to the listed exceptions.
quote: A contractor shall use this fiscal year as his cost accounting period, except that:

statement: The same cost accounting period is used to accumulate costs in an indirect cost pool and to establish its allocation base, except that the parties may agree to a different period for the base.
quote: The same cost accounting period shall be used for accumulating costs in an indirect cost pool as for establishing its allocation base, except that the contracting parties may agree to use a different period for establishing an allocation base as provided in 9904.406-50(e).

statement: A contractor must use a transitional cost accounting period of a length other than a year when its fiscal year changes.
quote: A transitional cost accounting period other than a year shall be used whenever a change of fiscal year occurs.

statement: Business unit general and administrative expenses are grouped in a separate indirect cost pool and allocated only to final cost objectives.
quote: Business unit G&A expenses shall be grouped in a separate indirect cost pool which shall be allocated only to final cost objectives.

statement: Except for final cost objectives subject to special allocation under (b)(2), the G&A expense pool of a business unit for a cost accounting period is allocated to final cost objectives of that period by a cost input base representing the business unit's total activity.
quote: The G&A expense pool of a business unit for a cost accounting period shall be allocated to final cost objectives of that cost accounting period by means of a cost input base representing the total activity of the business unit except as provided in subparagraph (b)(2) of this subsection.

statement: Final cost objectives that receive benefits significantly different from other final cost objectives get their G&A expense allocation by special allocation.
quote: The allocation of the G&A expense pool to any particular final cost objectives which receive benefits significantly different from the benefits accruing to other final cost objectives shall be determined by special allocation

statement: A business unit must have a written statement of accounting policies and practices for classifying costs as direct or indirect, consistently applied.
quote: A business unit shall have a written statement of accounting policies and practices for classifying costs as direct or indirect which shall be consistently applied.

statement: Indirect costs are accumulated in indirect cost pools that are homogeneous.
quote: Indirect costs shall be accumulated in indirect cost pools which are homogeneous.

statement: Pooled costs are allocated to cost objectives in reasonable proportion to the beneficial or causal relationship of the pooled costs to the cost objectives.
quote: Pooled costs shall be allocated to cost objectives in reasonable proportion to the beneficial or causal relationship of the pooled costs to cost objectives

statement: The only allowable advertising costs are those in the categories listed in 31.205-1(d); the first category is costs specifically required by contract, or arising from requirements of Government contracts, that are exclusively for acquiring scarce items for contract performance, and the rest of the list is in the next two claims.
quote: The only allowable advertising costs are those that are— (1) Specifically required by contract, or that arise from requirements of Government contracts, and that are exclusively for— (i) Acquiring scarce items for contract performance;
note: In RFO FAR 31.205-1, allowable advertising is renumbered from subsection (d) to subsection (c).

statement: Costs of activities to promote sales of products normally sold to the U.S. Government, including trade shows that contain a significant effort to promote exports from the United States, are an allowable category of advertising costs; the exclusions from that category are in a later claim.
quote: Costs of activities to promote sales of products normally sold to the U.S. Government, including trade shows, which contain a significant effort to promote exports from the United States.
note: Such costs exclude memorabilia, alcoholic beverages, entertainment, and physical facilities used primarily for entertainment.

statement: Public relations and advertising costs, other than those specified in paragraphs (d) and (e) of 31.205-1, whose primary purpose is to promote the sale of products or services by stimulating interest in a product or product line (except costs made allowable under 31.205-38(b)(5)), or by disseminating messages calling favorable attention to the contractor to enhance the company image to sell its products or services, are unallowable.
quote: All public relations and advertising costs, other than those specified in paragraphs (d) and (e) of this subsection, whose primary purpose is to promote the sale of products or services by stimulating interest in a product or product line (except for those costs made allowable under 31.205-38(b)(5))
note: In RFO FAR 31.205-1, unallowable costs are renumbered from subsection (f) to subsection (e).

statement: Bad debts, including actual or estimated losses arising from uncollectible accounts receivable due from customers and other claims, and any directly associated costs such as collection costs and legal costs, are unallowable.
quote: Bad debts, including actual or estimated losses arising from uncollectible accounts receivable due from customers and other claims, and any directly associated costs such as collection costs, and legal costs are unallowable.
note: RFO FAR 31.205-3 retains the exact same wording.

statement: Directly associated costs of bad debts, including collection costs and legal costs, are unallowable.
quote: directly associated costs such as collection costs, and legal costs are unallowable.
note: Costs directly associated with unallowable bad debts cannot be allocated to government contracts.

statement: Costs of fines and penalties resulting from violations of, or failure of the contractor to comply with, Federal, State, local, or foreign laws and regulations are unallowable, except when incurred as a result of compliance with specific terms and conditions of the contract; the next claim quotes the whole exception.
quote: Costs of fines and penalties resulting from violations of, or failure of the contractor to comply with, Federal, State, local, or foreign laws and regulations, are unallowable except when incurred as a result of compliance with specific terms and conditions of the contract
note: Fines and penalties are allowable only when incurred as a result of compliance with specific contract terms or written contracting officer instructions.

statement: Costs incurred in connection with, or related to, the mischarging of costs on Government contracts are unallowable when caused by, or resulting from, alteration or destruction of records, or other false or improper charging or recording of costs.
quote: Costs incurred in connection with, or related to, the mischarging of costs on Government contracts are unallowable when the costs are caused by, or result from, alteration or destruction of records, or other false or improper charging or recording of costs.
note: RFO FAR 31.205-15(b) contains the identical mischarging provision.

statement: Unallowable mischarging costs include costs incurred to measure or determine the magnitude of improper charging, and costs incurred to remedy or correct the mischarging, such as rescreening and reconstructing records.
quote: Such costs include those incurred to measure or otherwise determine the magnitude of the improper charging, and costs incurred to remedy or correct the mischarging, such as costs to rescreen and reconstruct records.
note: Corrective and measurement costs stemming from improper charging or record alteration cannot be charged to the government.

statement: Interest on borrowings (however represented), bond discounts, costs of financing and refinancing capital (net worth plus long-term liabilities), legal and professional fees paid in connection with preparing prospectuses, and costs of preparing and issuing stock rights are unallowable, subject to the cross-reference and the exception stated in the next claim.
quote: Interest on borrowings (however represented), bond discounts, costs of financing and refinancing capital (net worth plus long-term liabilities), legal and professional fees paid in connection with preparing prospectuses, and costs of preparing and issuing stock rights are unallowable
note: In RFO FAR 31.205-20, these unallowable financial costs are itemized in paragraph (a).

statement: Interest assessed by State or local taxing authorities is allowable only under the conditions specified in 31.205-41(a)(3).
quote: However, interest assessed by State or local taxing authorities under the conditions specified in 31.205-41(a)(3) is allowable.
note: In RFO FAR 31.205-20(b), the taxing authority interest rule references 31.205-41(b)(3).

statement: Costs associated with attempts to influence the outcomes of any Federal, State, or local election, referendum, initiative, or similar procedure, through in kind or cash contributions, endorsements, publicity, or similar activities, are unallowable.
quote: Attempts to influence the outcomes of any Federal, State, or local election, referendum, initiative, or similar procedure, through in kind or cash contributions, endorsements, publicity, or similar activities;
note: RFO FAR 31.205-22(a)(1) contains the same prohibition using in-kind.

statement: Providing a technical and factual presentation of information on a topic directly related to the performance of a contract, through hearing testimony, statements or letters to the Congress or a state legislature, is excepted from the lobbying costs made unallowable by paragraph (a), on the conditions stated in the next claims.
quote: Providing a technical and factual presentation of information on a topic directly related to the performance of a contract through hearing testimony, statements or letters to the Congress or a state legislature
note: RFO FAR 31.205-22(b)(1) retains the technical and factual presentation exception.

statement: When a contractor seeks reimbursement for indirect costs, total lobbying costs must be separately identified in the indirect cost rate proposal and thereafter treated as other unallowable activity costs.
quote: When a contractor seeks reimbursement for indirect costs, total lobbying costs shall be separately identified in the indirect cost rate proposal, and thereafter treated as other unallowable activity costs.
note: RFO FAR 31.205-22(c) uses must instead of shall.

statement: Contractors must maintain adequate records to demonstrate that the certification of costs as being allowable or unallowable complies with the lobbying cost principle requirements.
quote: Contractors shall maintain adequate records to demonstrate that the certification of costs as being allowable or unallowable (see 42.703-2) pursuant to this subsection complies with the requirements of this subsection.
note: RFO FAR 31.205-22(d) refers to this section rather than this subsection.

statement: Contributions or donations, including cash, property and services, regardless of recipient, are unallowable, except as provided in 31.205-1(e)(3).
quote: Contributions or donations, including cash, property and services, regardless of recipient, are unallowable
note: The RFO text keeps the same bar and the same recipient-neutral scope.

statement: The only exception is external to the section: allowability turns on the separate provision the section cross-references, not on anything stated in the section itself.
quote: regardless of recipient, are unallowable, except as provided in 31.205-1(e)(3).
note: The codified text points to 31.205-1(e)(3); the RFO text points to 31.205-1(d)(3) instead.

statement: Costs of activities designed to improve working conditions, employer-employee relations, employee morale or employee performance are allowable in the aggregate, less the income those activities generate, and remain subject to the limitations in the subsection.
quote: Aggregate costs incurred on activities designed to improve working conditions, employer-employee relations, employee morale, and employee performance (less income generated by these activities) are allowable, subject to the limitations contained in this subsection.
note: The RFO text keeps the same aggregate test and the same limitations.

statement: Gifts are unallowable, but awards for performance and awards recognising employee achievements under an established contractor plan or policy are not gifts.
quote: Costs of gifts are unallowable. (Gifts do not include awards for performance made pursuant to 31.205-6(f) or awards made in recognition of employee achievements pursuant to an established contractor plan or policy.)
note: The RFO text splits the gift rule into (b)(1) and (b)(2) and points to 31.205-6(e) for performance awards.

statement: Recreation costs are unallowable, except for employee participation in company sponsored sports teams or employee organizations designed to improve company loyalty, team work or physical fitness.
quote: Costs of recreation are unallowable, except for the costs of employees' participation in company sponsored sports teams or employee organizations designed to improve company loyalty, team work, or physical fitness.

statement: Losses from operating food and dormitory services are allowable only if the contractor's objective is to operate those services on a break-even basis.
quote: Losses from operating food and dormitory services are allowable only if the contractor's objective is to operate such services on a break-even basis.

statement: Except as provided in paragraph (b), expenditures in connection with planning or executing the organization or reorganization of the corporate structure of a business, including mergers and acquisitions, are the first of three categories in one sentence, which closes by declaring the listed expenditures unallowable (quoted in the claim on raising capital).
quote: Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, expenditures in connection with (1) planning or executing the organization or reorganization of the corporate structure of a business, including mergers and acquisitions
note: The RFO text restructures codified paragraph (a) into subparagraphs (a)(1)(i) through (a)(1)(iii).

statement: Expenditures in connection with resisting or planning to resist a reorganization of the corporate structure or a change in the controlling interest in the ownership of a business are the second of the three categories in that sentence, which closes by declaring the listed expenditures unallowable (quoted in the claim on raising capital); the lead-in and the paragraph (b) exception are quoted in the claim on the first category.
quote: resisting or planning to resist the reorganization of the corporate structure of a business or a change in the controlling interest in the ownership of a business

statement: The sentence closes by stating that the expenditures it lists, including those in connection with raising capital (net worth plus long-term liabilities), are unallowable.
quote: raising capital (net worth plus long-term liabilities), are unallowable

statement: The bar reaches the professional fees around those transactions, including incorporation fees and the costs of attorneys, accountants, brokers, promoters, organizers, management consultants and investment counselors, whether or not they are the contractor's employees.
quote: Such expenditures include but are not limited to incorporation fees and costs of attorneys, accountants, brokers, promoters and organizers, management consultants and investment counselors, whether or not employees of the contractor.

statement: Unallowable reorganization costs include a change in the contractor's financial structure that alters the rights and interests of security holders, whether or not additional capital is raised, but exclude the administrative costs of short-term borrowings for working capital.
quote: include the cost of any change in the contractor's financial structure, excluding administrative costs of short-term borrowings for working capital, resulting in alterations in the rights and interests of security holders, whether or not additional capital is raised.

statement: The cost of activities primarily intended to provide compensation is not organization cost; the section sends it to the compensation principle instead.
quote: The cost of activities primarily intended to provide compensation will not be considered organizational costs subject to this subsection, but will be governed by 31.205-6.
note: The RFO text keeps the carve-out and still cross-references 31.205-6.

statement: The printed examples of compensation activity are acquiring stock for executive bonuses, employee savings plans and employee stock ownership plans.
quote: These activities include acquiring stock for (1) executive bonuses, (2) employee savings plans, and (3) employee stock ownership plans.

statement: Memberships in trade, business, technical and professional organizations are an allowable type of cost.
quote: The following types of costs are allowable: (a) Memberships in trade, business, technical, and professional organizations.
note: The RFO text keeps the same three allowable categories in the same order.

statement: Subscriptions to trade, business, professional or other technical periodicals are allowable.
quote: Subscriptions to trade, business, professional, or other technical periodicals.

statement: When the principal purpose of a meeting, convention, conference, symposium or seminar is the dissemination of trade, business, technical or professional information or the stimulation of production or improved productivity, the costs listed in paragraphs (c)(1) to (c)(3), such as organizing and sponsoring costs and attendance costs, are allowable, subject to the conditions stated for each.
quote: When the principal purpose of a meeting, convention, conference, symposium, or seminar is the dissemination of trade, business, technical or professional information or the stimulation of production or improved productivity

statement: Within that purpose test, the costs of organizing, setting up and sponsoring the event, including rental of meeting facilities, transportation, subsistence and incidental costs, are allowable.
quote: Costs of organizing, setting up, and sponsoring the meetings, conventions, symposia, etc., including rental of meeting facilities, transportation, subsistence, and incidental costs

statement: Costs of attendance by contractor employees, including travel costs, are an allowable type of cost, with travel cross-referenced to the separate travel section.
quote: Costs of attendance by contractor employees, including travel costs (see 31.205-46)

statement: For attendance by people who are not contractor employees, the cost must not also be reimbursed to the individual by the employing company or organization.
quote: Such costs are not also reimbursed to the individual by the employing company or organization

statement: The second condition for non-employee attendance is that the individual's attendance is essential to achieve the purpose of the conference, meeting, convention or symposium.
quote: The individual's attendance is essential to achieve the purpose of the conference, meeting, convention, symposium, etc.

statement: The cost of alcoholic beverages is unallowable, and the section states no exception to that bar.
quote: Costs of alcoholic beverages are unallowable. [51 FR 12302, Apr. 9, 1986]
note: The RFO text repeats the bar without change.

statement: An acceptable accounting system must provide reasonable assurance that contract allocations and charges are consistent with billing procedures.
quote: Contract allocations and charges are consistent with billing procedures

statement: An accounting system is the contractor's system or systems for accounting methods, procedures and controls established to gather, record, classify, analyze, summarize, interpret and present accurate and timely financial data.
quote: the Contractor's system or systems for accounting methods, procedures, and controls established to gather, record, classify, analyze, summarize, interpret, and present accurate and timely financial data

statement: Failure to maintain an acceptable accounting system results in withholding of payments when the contract includes the Contractor Business Systems clause, and may also result in disapproval of the system.
quote: Failure to maintain an acceptable accounting system, as defined in this clause, shall result in the withholding of payments if the contract includes the clause at 252.242-7005, Contractor Business Systems, and also may result in disapproval of the system.

statement: The accounting system must provide for a sound internal control environment, an accounting framework and an organizational structure.
quote: A sound internal control environment, accounting framework, and organizational structure

statement: The system must use a logical and consistent method for accumulating and allocating indirect costs to intermediate and final cost objectives.
quote: A logical and consistent method for the accumulation and allocation of indirect costs to intermediate and final cost objectives

statement: The system must reconcile subsidiary cost ledgers and cost objectives to the general ledger.
quote: Reconciliation of subsidiary cost ledgers and cost objectives to general ledger

statement: The system must include a timekeeping system that identifies employees' labor by intermediate or final cost objectives.
quote: A timekeeping system that identifies employees' labor by intermediate or final cost objectives

statement: The system must provide for interim determination, at least monthly, of costs charged to a contract through routine posting of books of account.
quote: Interim (at least monthly) determination of costs charged to a contract through routine posting of books of account

statement: The system must exclude from costs charged to Government contracts amounts that are not allowable under the cost principles in the Federal Acquisition Regulation and other contract provisions.
quote: Exclusion from costs charged to Government contracts of amounts which are not allowable in terms of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) part 31

statement: The system must produce billings that reconcile to the cost accounts for both current and cumulative amounts claimed and that comply with contract terms.
quote: Billings that can be reconciled to the cost accounts for both current and cumulative amounts claimed and comply with contract terms

statement: Accounting practices must follow standards promulgated by the Cost Accounting Standards Board when applicable and otherwise generally accepted accounting principles.
quote: Accounting practices in accordance with standards promulgated by the Cost Accounting Standards Board, if applicable, otherwise, Generally Accepted Accounting Principles

statement: The contractor must respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the contracting officer that identifies material weaknesses in its accounting system.
quote: The Contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the Contracting Officer that identifies material weaknesses in the Contractor's accounting system.

statement: After a final determination of material weaknesses, the contractor must within 45 days of receipt either correct the weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan.
quote: within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the material weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan

statement: If the contracting officer makes a final determination to disapprove the contractor's accounting system and the contract includes the Contractor Business Systems clause, the contracting officer withholds payments in accordance with that clause.
quote: the Contracting Officer will withhold payments in accordance with that clause

statement: Compensation for personal services must be for work performed by the employee in the current year and must not represent a retroactive adjustment of prior years' salaries or wages, subject to the cross-referenced exceptions in paragraphs (g), (h), (j), (k), (m), and (o) of the cost principle.
quote: Compensation for personal services must be for work performed by the employee in the current year and must not represent a retroactive adjustment of prior years' salaries or wages (but see paragraphs (g), (h), (j), (k), (m), and (o) of this subsection).

statement: The total compensation for individual employees or job classes of employees must be reasonable for the work performed; however, specific restrictions on individual compensation elements apply when prescribed.
quote: The total compensation for individual employees or job classes of employees must be reasonable for the work performed; however, specific restrictions on individual compensation elements apply when prescribed.

statement: No presumption of allowability will exist where the contractor introduces major revisions of existing compensation plans or new plans and has not provided the cognizant ACO the opportunity described in the rest of the sentence, which the next claim quotes.
quote: No presumption of allowability will exist where the contractor introduces major revisions of existing compensation plans or new plans and the contractor has not provided the cognizant ACO
note: The RFO text names the reviewing official the cognizant administrative contracting officer rather than the cognizant ACO.

statement: For owners of closely held companies, compensation in excess of the costs deductible as compensation under the Internal Revenue Code and its regulations is unallowable.
quote: For owners of closely held companies, compensation in excess of the costs that are deductible as compensation under the Internal Revenue Code (26 U.S.C.) and regulations under it is unallowable

statement: Costs of training and education related to the field in which the employee is working or may reasonably be expected to work are allowable, except as the cost principle otherwise lists.
quote: Costs of training and education that are related to the field in which the employee is working or may reasonably be expected to work are allowable, except as follows:

statement: The cost of salaries for attending undergraduate level classes or part-time graduate level classes during working hours is unallowable, except when unusual circumstances do not permit attendance outside regular working hours.
quote: The cost of salaries for attending undergraduate level classes or part-time graduate level classes during working hours is unallowable, except when unusual circumstances do not permit attendance at such classes outside of regular working hours.

statement: Costs in connection with full-time graduate level education are unallowable for any portion of the program that exceeds two school years or the length of the degree program, whichever is less.
quote: full-time graduate level education are unallowable for any portion of the program that exceeds two school years or the length of the degree program, whichever is less

statement: Costs of professional and consultant services are allowable, subject to paragraphs (b) through (f) of the cost principle (but see 31.205-30 and 31.205-47), when reasonable in relation to the services rendered and when not contingent upon recovery of the costs from the Government.
quote: Costs of professional and consultant services are allowable subject to this paragraph and paragraphs (c) through (f) of this subsection when reasonable in relation to the services rendered and when not contingent upon recovery of the costs from the Government

statement: Costs of professional and consultant services are unallowable when the services are intended to improperly influence the contents of solicitations, the evaluation of proposals or quotations, or the selection of sources for contract award.
quote: Services that are intended to improperly influence the contents of solicitations, the evaluation of proposals or quotations, or the selection of sources for contract award, whether award is by the Government, or by a prime contractor or subcontractor.

statement: Retainer fees are allowable only when supported by evidence that the covered services are necessary and customary, that the level of past services justifies the amount, that the fee is reasonable compared with an in-house capability, and that the actual services performed are documented.
quote: (1) The services covered by the retainer agreement are necessary and customary

statement: Rental costs under operating leases are allowable to the extent the rates are reasonable at the time of the lease decision, after considering factors such as comparable property, market conditions, and the type and condition of the property.
quote: Rental costs under operating leases, to the extent that the rates are reasonable at the time of the lease decision, after consideration of

statement: This subsection applies to the cost of renting or leasing real or personal property acquired under operating leases.
quote: This subsection is applicable to the cost of renting or leasing real or personal property acquired under “operating leases”

statement: Rental costs under a sale and leaseback arrangement are allowable only up to the amount the contractor would be allowed if the contractor retained title.
quote: Rental costs under a sale and leaseback arrangement only up to the amount the contractor would be allowed if the contractor retained title

statement: Depreciation on a contractor's plant, equipment, and other capital facilities is an allowable contract cost, subject to the limitations in this cost principle.
quote: Depreciation on a contractor's plant, equipment, and other capital facilities is an allowable contract cost, subject to the limitations contained in this cost principle

statement: For tangible personal property, only estimated residual values that exceed 10 percent of the capitalized cost of the asset need be used in establishing depreciable costs.
quote: For tangible personal property, only estimated residual values that exceed 10 percent of the capitalized cost of the asset need be used in establishing depreciable costs

statement: Depreciation, rental, or use charges are unallowable on property acquired from the Government at no cost by the contractor or by any division, subsidiary, or affiliate of the contractor under common control.
quote: Depreciation, rental, or use charges are unallowable on property acquired from the Government at no cost by the contractor or by any division, subsidiary, or affiliate of the contractor under common control.

statement: No depreciation or rental is allowed on property fully depreciated by the contractor or by any division, subsidiary, or affiliate of the contractor under common control; however, a reasonable charge for using fully depreciated property may be agreed upon and allowed.
quote: No depreciation or rental is allowed on property fully depreciated by the contractor or by any division, subsidiary, or affiliate of the contractor under common control. However, a reasonable charge for using fully depreciated property may be agreed upon and allowed (but, see 31.109(h)(2)).

statement: Costs of insurance required or approved pursuant to the contract are allowable under FAR cost principles.
quote: Costs of insurance required or approved pursuant to the contract are allowable.

statement: If purchased insurance is available, any self-insurance charge plus insurance administration expenses in excess of the cost of comparable purchased insurance plus associated administration expenses is unallowable.
quote: If purchased insurance is available, any self-insurance charge plus insurance administration expenses in excess of the cost of comparable purchased insurance plus associated insurance administration expenses is unallowable.

statement: Actual losses are unallowable unless expressly provided for in the contract, except that losses incurred under the nominal deductible provisions of purchased insurance in keeping with sound business practice, and minor losses in the ordinary course of business that are not covered by insurance (such as spoilage, breakage, and disappearance of small hand tools), are allowable.
quote: Actual losses are unallowable unless expressly provided for in the contract, except— (i) Losses incurred under the nominal deductible provisions of purchased insurance, in keeping with sound business practice, are allowable;

statement: Costs not covered elsewhere in the legal proceedings cost principle are unallowable if incurred in connection with defense against Federal Government claims or appeals or the prosecution of claims or appeals against the Federal Government.
quote: Costs not covered elsewhere in this subsection are unallowable if incurred in connection with the following— (1) Defense against Federal Government claims or appeals or the prosecution of claims or appeals against the Federal Government (see 2.101).

statement: For costs incurred in connection with proceedings described in paragraph (b) but not made unallowable by it, the percentage of costs allowed may not exceed 80 percent, and agreements under paragraph (c) are subject to that limit.
quote: Such percentage shall not exceed 80 percent. Agreements reached under paragraph (c) of this subsection shall be subject to this limitation.

statement: Costs that may be unallowable under the legal proceedings cost principle, including directly associated costs, must be segregated and accounted for separately by the contractor or subcontractor.
quote: Costs which may be unallowable under 31.205-47, including directly associated costs, shall be segregated and accounted for by the contractor or subcontractor separately.

statement: Any costs for amortization, expensing, write-off, or write-down of goodwill, however represented, are unallowable.
quote: Any costs for amortization, expensing, write-off, or write-down of goodwill (however represented) are unallowable.

statement: Goodwill originates under the purchase method of accounting for a business combination when the purchase price exceeds the fair value of net identifiable assets acquired.
quote: originates under the purchase method of accounting for a business combination when the price paid by the acquiring company exceeds the sum of the identifiable individual assets acquired less liabilities assumed, based upon their fair values.

statement: Goodwill may arise from the acquisition of a company as a whole or a portion of a company.
quote: Goodwill may arise from the acquisition of a company as a whole or a portion thereof.

statement: Gains and losses from the sale, retirement, or other disposition of depreciable property (but see 31.205-19) are included in the year in which they occur as credits or charges to the cost groupings described in the next claim.
quote: Gains and losses from the sale, retirement, or other disposition (but see 31.205-19) of depreciable property shall be included in the year in which they occur as credits or charges to the cost grouping(s)

statement: Gains and losses of any nature arising from the sale or exchange of capital assets other than depreciable property are excluded in computing contract costs.
quote: Gains and losses of any nature arising from the sale or exchange of capital assets other than depreciable property shall be excluded in computing contract costs.

statement: No loss is allowed for a write-down from carrying value to fair value of long-lived tangible and identifiable intangible assets held for use resulting from impairments caused by events or changes in circumstances.
quote: With respect to long-lived tangible and identifiable intangible assets held for use, no loss shall be allowed for a write-down from carrying value to fair value as a result of impairments caused by events or changes in circumstances

statement: Material costs include items such as raw materials, parts, subassemblies, components, and manufacturing supplies, and may include collateral items like inbound transportation and in-transit insurance.
quote: Material costs include the costs of such items as raw materials, parts, subassemblies, components, and manufacturing supplies, whether purchased or manufactured by the contractor, and may include such collateral items as inbound transportation and in-transit insurance.

statement: A contractor must adjust material costs for income and other credits, including available trade discounts, refunds, rebates, allowances, and cash discounts, and credits for scrap, salvage, and material returned to vendors.
quote: The contractor shall— (1) Adjust the costs of material for income and other credits, including available trade discounts, refunds, rebates, allowances, and cash discounts, and credits for scrap, salvage, and material returned to vendors;

statement: Allowance for materials, supplies, and services transferred between divisions, subdivisions, subsidiaries, or affiliates under common control is on the basis of cost incurred, but may be at price when it is the established practice to price such transfers at other than cost for commercial work, the item qualifies for an exception under 15.403-1(b), and the contracting officer has not determined the price to be unreasonable.
quote: Allowance for all materials, supplies and services that are sold or transferred between any divisions, subdivisions, subsidiaries, or affiliates of the contractor under a common control shall be on the basis of cost incurred in accordance with this subpart.

statement: An advance agreement is not an absolute requirement and the absence of an advance agreement on any cost will not in itself affect the reasonableness, allocability, or allowability of that cost.
quote: an advance agreement is not an absolute requirement and the absence of an advance agreement on any cost will not, in itself, affect the reasonableness, allocability or the allowability under the specific cost principles

statement: Advance agreements must be in writing, executed by both contracting parties, incorporated into applicable contracts, and state their applicability and duration.
quote: The agreements must be in writing, executed by both contracting parties, and incorporated into applicable current and future contracts. An advance agreement shall contain a statement of its applicability and duration.

statement: A contracting officer is not authorized to agree to a treatment of costs inconsistent with the contract cost principles, such as agreeing that interest is allowable.
quote: The contracting officer is not authorized by this 31.109 to agree to a treatment of costs inconsistent with this part. For example, an advance agreement may not provide that, notwithstanding 31.205-20, interest is allowable.

statement: Home office expenses are allocated on the basis of the beneficial or causal relationship between the supporting activity and the segment that receives it.
quote: Home office expenses shall be allocated on the basis of the beneficial or causal relationship between supporting and receiving activities.

statement: Home office expenses are allocated directly to segments to the maximum extent practical; only expenses not directly allocated, if significant in amount and in relation to total home office expenses, are grouped in pools.
quote: Such expenses shall be allocated directly to segments to the maximum extent practical.

statement: A segment may not be charged a cost as an indirect cost through a homogeneous expense pool or the residual pool if other costs incurred for the same purpose were allocated directly to a segment.
quote: any cost, if other costs incurred for the same purpose have been allocated directly to that or any other segment.

statement: Expenses of a home office centralized service function are allocated to segments on the basis of the service furnished to or received by each segment.
quote: Expenses of centralized service functions performed by a home office for its segments shall be allocated to segments on the basis of the service furnished to or received by each segment.

statement: Residual home office expenses are allocated to all segments under a base representative of the total activity of those segments, except where the special rules in the section apply.
quote: Residual expenses shall be allocated to all segments under a home office by means of a base representative of the total activity of such segments, except where paragraph (c) (2) or (3) of this subsection applies.

statement: Residual expenses are allocated pursuant to 9904.403-50(c)(1) if the previous fiscal year's total residual expenses (excluding unallowable costs and before eliminating amounts specially allocated under (c)(3)) exceed the amount obtained by applying 3.35% of the first $100 million, 0.95% of the next $200 million, 0.30% of the next $2.7 billion and 0.20% of amounts over $3 billion to the aggregate revenue of all segments for that year.
quote: 3.35 percent of the first $100 million; 0.95 percent of the next $200 million; 0.30 percent of the next $2.7 billion; 0.20 percent of all amounts over $3 billion.

statement: For a defined-benefit plan other than one using the pay-as-you-go method, pension cost includes normal cost, part of any unfunded actuarial liability, an interest equivalent on the unamortized liability and an adjustment for actuarial gains and losses.
quote: the components of pension cost for a cost accounting period are (i) the normal cost of the period, (ii) a part of any unfunded actuarial liability, (iii) an interest equivalent on the unamortized portion of any unfunded actuarial liability, and (iv) an adjustment for any actuarial gains and losses.

statement: For a defined-contribution plan, pension cost is the net contribution required for the period, after dividends and other credits where applicable.
quote: For defined-contribution pension plans, the pension cost for a cost accounting period is the net contribution required to be made for that period, after taking into account dividends and other credits, where applicable.

statement: For a defined-benefit plan outside the pay-as-you-go method, pension cost is determined using an immediate-gain actuarial cost method.
quote: the amount of pension cost of a cost accounting period shall be determined by use of an immediate-gain actuarial cost method.

statement: Each actuarial assumption used to measure pension cost must be separately identified and must be the contractor's best estimate of anticipated experience under the plan, judged on its own.
quote: Each actuarial assumption used to measure pension cost shall be separately identified and shall represent the contractor's best estimates of anticipated experience under the plan, taking into account past experience and reasonable expectations.

statement: Pension cost computed for a cost accounting period is assignable only to that period, apart from costs the standard allows to be assigned to future periods.
quote: the amount of pension cost computed for a cost accounting period is assignable only to that period.

statement: Actuarial gains and losses are calculated annually and assigned to the period for which the valuation is made and to later periods.
quote: Actuarial gains and losses shall be calculated annually and shall be assigned to the cost accounting period for which the actuarial valuation is made and subsequent periods.

statement: The actuarial value of the assets of a pension plan must be determined under an asset valuation method that takes into account unrealized appreciation and depreciation of the market value of the plan assets, as further stated in the next claim.
quote: The actuarial value of the assets of a pension plan shall be determined under an asset valuation method which takes into account unrealized appreciation and depreciation of the market value of the assets of the pension plan

statement: Pension cost is allocated to each segment that has participants in a pension plan.
quote: Contractors shall allocate pension costs to each segment having participants in a pension plan.

statement: A separate pension cost calculation for a segment is required when the stated conditions are present; otherwise a composite cost may be allocated by an allocation base.
quote: A separate calculation of pension costs for a segment is required when the conditions set forth in 9904.413-50(c)(2) or (3) are present.

statement: Where pension cost is separately computed for a segment, the amount assignable to that segment may not exceed a ceiling that includes the maximum tax-deductible amount computed for the plan as a whole.
quote: the amount of pension cost assignable to a segment or segments shall not exceed the sum of: (i) The maximum tax-deductible amount computed for the plan as a whole

statement: Facilities capital is measured and allocated under the standard, and the allocated amount is the base to which a cost of money rate is applied.
quote: A contractor's facilities capital shall be measured and allocated in accordance with the criteria set forth in this Standard. The allocated amount shall be used as a base to which a cost of money rate is applied.

statement: The cost of money rate is based on rates determined by the Secretary of the Treasury under the public law named in the standard.
quote: The cost of money rate shall be based on rates determined by the Secretary of the Treasury, pursuant to Public Law 92-41 (85 stat. 97).

statement: The cost of capital committed to facilities is computed separately for each contract using facilities capital cost of money factors computed for each cost accounting period.
quote: The cost of capital committed to facilities shall be separately computed for each contract using facilities capital cost of money factors computed for each cost accounting period.

statement: Deferred compensation cost is assigned to the period in which the contractor incurs the obligation to compensate the employee.
quote: The cost of deferred compensation shall be assigned to the cost accounting period in which the contractor incurs an obligation to compensate the employee.

statement: If no obligation is incurred before payment, the cost is the amount paid and is assigned to the period in which the payment is made.
quote: In the event no obligation is incurred prior to payment, the cost of deferred compensation shall be the amount paid and shall be assigned to the cost accounting period in which the payment is made.

statement: For deferred compensation other than an ESOP, the cost is the present value of the future benefits to be paid by the contractor.
quote: For deferred compensation other than ESOPs, the deferred compensation cost shall be the present value of the future benefits to be paid by the contractor.

statement: For an ESOP, the cost is the amount contributed to the ESOP by the contractor.
quote: For an ESOP, the deferred compensation cost shall be the amount contributed to the ESOP by the contractor.

statement: Each award of deferred compensation is measured and assigned separately, but group measurement is allowed where it is reasonably accurate for the employees covered by the plan.
quote: if the cost of deferred compensation for the employees covered by a deferred compensation plan can be measured and assigned with reasonable accuracy on a group basis, separate computations for each employee are not required.

statement: The unit for identifying and accumulating independent research and development and bid and proposal cost is the individual project.
quote: The basic unit for the identification and accumulation of Independent Research and Development (IR&D) and Bid and Proposal (B&P) costs shall be the individual IR&D or B&P project.

statement: Independent research and development and bid and proposal project cost consists of all allocable costs except business unit general and administrative expense.
quote: The IR&D and B&P project costs shall consist of all allocable costs, except business unit general and administrative expenses.

statement: A home office's independent research and development and bid and proposal pools are allocated to segments on the basis of beneficial or causal relationship.
quote: The IR&D and B&P cost pools of a home office shall be allocated to segments on the basis of the beneficial or causal relationship between the IR&D and B&P costs and the segments reporting to that home office.

statement: A business unit's independent research and development and bid and proposal pools are allocated to that unit's final cost objectives on the basis of beneficial or causal relationship.
quote: allocated to the final cost objectives of that business unit on the basis of the beneficial or causal relationship between the IR&D and B&P costs and the final cost objectives

statement: Bid and proposal cost incurred in a cost accounting period is not assigned to any other cost accounting period.
quote: The B&P costs incurred in a cost accounting period shall not be assigned to any other cost accounting period.

statement: Independent research and development cost is not assigned to another period either, except as existing laws, regulations and other controlling factors permit.
quote: The IR&D costs incurred in a cost accounting period shall not be assigned to any other cost accounting period, except as may be permitted pursuant to provisions of existing laws, regulations, and other controlling factors.

statement: Records include books, documents, accounting procedures and practices, and other data, regardless of type or form.
quote: records includes books, documents, accounting procedures and practices, and other data, regardless of type and regardless of whether such items are in written form, in the form of computer data, or in any other form.

statement: The cost-examination provision covers cost-reimbursement, incentive, time-and-materials, labor-hour, and price redeterminable contracts, including combinations of those types.
quote: If this is a cost-reimbursement, incentive, time-and-materials, labor-hour, or price redeterminable contract, or any combination of these,

statement: For covered contracts, the contractor must maintain records and other evidence sufficient to reflect properly costs claimed to have been incurred, and the Contracting Officer or an authorized representative may examine and audit them.
quote: the Contractor shall maintain and the Contracting Officer, or an authorized representative of the Contracting Officer, shall have the right to examine and audit all records and other evidence sufficient to reflect properly all costs claimed to have been incurred

statement: The examination right includes inspection at all reasonable times of the contractor's plants, or parts of them, engaged in performing the contract.
quote: This right of examination shall include inspection at all reasonable times of the Contractor's plants, or parts of them, engaged in performing the contract.

statement: When certified cost or pricing data has been required, the examination and audit right covers related contractor records, including computations and projections, to evaluate accuracy, completeness, and currency.
quote: in order to evaluate the accuracy, completeness, and currency of the certified cost or pricing data, shall have the right to examine and audit all of the Contractor's records, including computations and projections

statement: Unless the contract is exempt under the cited CAS exemption provisions, the clause incorporates the CAS contract requirements by reference.
quote: Unless the contract is exempt under 48 CFR 9903.201-1 and 9903.201-2, the provisions of 48 CFR part 9903 are incorporated herein by reference

statement: Under the clause, a contractor on a CAS-covered contract discloses its cost accounting practices in a Disclosure Statement as required by 48 CFR 9903.202-1 through 9903.202-5, including methods of distinguishing direct costs from indirect costs and the basis used for allocating indirect costs.
quote: By submission of a Disclosure Statement, disclose in writing the Contractor's cost accounting practices as required by 48 CFR 9903.202-1 through 9903.202-5, including methods of distinguishing direct costs from indirect costs and the basis used for allocating indirect costs.

statement: The contractor must follow its cost accounting practices consistently in accumulating and reporting contract performance cost data for the contract.
quote: Follow consistently the Contractor's cost accounting practices in accumulating and reporting contract performance cost data concerning this contract.

statement: A change in cost accounting practices for a contract or subcontract subject to CAS requirements must be applied prospectively, and the Disclosure Statement must be amended accordingly.
quote: If any change in cost accounting practices is made for the purposes of any contract or subcontract subject to CAS requirements, the change must be applied prospectively to this contract and the Disclosure Statement must be amended accordingly.

statement: If the Contractor has notified the Contracting Officer that the Disclosure Statement contains trade secrets and commercial or financial information that is privileged and confidential, the Disclosure Statement must be protected and must not be released outside the Government.
quote: If the Contractor has notified the Contracting Officer that the Disclosure Statement contains trade secrets and commercial or financial information which is privileged and confidential, the Disclosure Statement shall be protected and shall not be released outside of the Government.

statement: For administering CAS requirements under the contract, the contractor must take the steps outlined in paragraphs (b) through (i) and (k) through (n) of the clause.
quote: For the purpose of administering the Cost Accounting Standards (CAS) requirements under this contract, the Contractor shall take the steps outlined in paragraphs (b) through (i) and (k) through (n) of this clause

statement: An affected CAS-covered contract or subcontract includes one where one practice was used to estimate costs and a changed practice was used to accumulate and report costs.
quote: Used one cost accounting practice to estimate costs and a changed cost accounting practice to accumulate and report costs under the contract or subcontract

statement: An affected CAS-covered contract or subcontract also includes one where a noncompliant practice was used for estimating or accumulating and reporting costs.
quote: Used a noncompliant practice for purposes of estimating or accumulating and reporting costs under the contract or subcontract

statement: The cognizant Federal agency official is the Contracting Officer assigned by the cognizant Federal agency to administer CAS.
