quote: Cognizant Federal agency official (CFAO) means the Contracting Officer assigned by the cognizant Federal agency to administer the CAS.

statement: A desirable change is a compliant change to established or disclosed cost accounting practices that the cognizant Federal agency official finds desirable and not detrimental to the Government.
quote: Desirable change means a compliant change to a Contractor's established or disclosed cost accounting practices that the CFAO finds is desirable and not detrimental to the Government

quote: before issuing the notice, the contracting officer responsible for administering the contract shall make every reasonable effort to reach a satisfactory settlement through discussions with the contractor.

statement: Price analysis is used when certified cost or pricing data are not required.
quote: Price analysis shall be used when certified cost or pricing data are not required

statement: Cost analysis is used to evaluate the reasonableness of individual cost elements when certified cost or pricing data are required.
quote: Cost analysis shall be used to evaluate the reasonableness of individual cost elements when certified cost or pricing data are required.

statement: Cost analysis may also be used on data other than certified cost or pricing data to determine cost reasonableness or cost realism when a fair and reasonable price cannot be determined through price analysis alone.
quote: Cost analysis may also be used to evaluate data other than certified cost or pricing data to determine cost reasonableness or cost realism when a fair and reasonable price cannot be determined through price analysis alone.

statement: The first two price analysis techniques are the preferred techniques, but if information on competitive proposed prices or previous contract prices is unavailable or insufficient to establish a fair and reasonable price, the contracting officer may use any of the remaining techniques.
quote: information on competitive proposed prices or previous contract prices is not available or is insufficient to determine that the price is fair and reasonable, the contracting officer may use any of the remaining techniques as appropriate to the circumstances applicable to the acquisition.

statement: Cost realism analyses are performed on cost-reimbursement contracts to determine the probable cost of performance for each offeror.
quote: Cost realism analyses shall be performed on cost-reimbursement contracts to determine the probable cost of performance for each offeror.

statement: The probable cost produced by cost realism analysis is used for purposes of evaluation to determine the best value.
quote: The probable cost shall be used for purposes of evaluation to determine the best value.

statement: Where cost realism analysis is used on competitive fixed-price incentive contracts or on other competitive fixed-price-type contracts, the proposals are still evaluated using the criteria in the solicitation and the offered prices are not adjusted as a result of the analysis.
quote: proposals shall be evaluated using the criteria in the solicitation, and the offered prices shall not be adjusted as a result of the analysis

statement: Recommendations or conclusions about the Government's review of a proposal are not disclosed to the offeror or contractor without the concurrence of the contracting officer.
quote: Recommendations or conclusions regarding the Government's review or analysis of an offeror's or contractor's proposal shall not be disclosed to the offeror or contractor without the concurrence of the contracting officer

statement: Normally, adequate price competition establishes a fair and reasonable price.
quote: Normally, adequate price competition establishes a fair and reasonable price

statement: An offer may be rejected if the contracting officer determines that the lack of price balance poses an unacceptable risk to the Government.
quote: An offer may be rejected if the contracting officer determines that the lack of balance poses an unacceptable risk to the Government.

statement: An acceptable estimating system must produce verifiable, supportable, documented and timely cost estimates that are an acceptable basis for negotiation of fair and reasonable prices, in addition to being maintained, reliable and consistently applied.
quote: (1) Is maintained, reliable, and consistently applied; (2) Produces verifiable, supportable, documented, and timely cost estimates that are an acceptable basis for negotiation of fair and reasonable prices

statement: An estimating system is the contractor's policies, procedures and practices for budgeting and planning controls and for generating estimates of costs and other data included in proposals submitted in the expectation of receiving contract awards.
quote: the Contractor's policies, procedures, and practices for budgeting and planning controls, and generating estimates of costs and other data included in proposals submitted to customers in the expectation of receiving contract awards.

statement: The contractor must establish, maintain and comply with an acceptable estimating system.
quote: The Contractor shall establish, maintain, and comply with an acceptable estimating system.

statement: One condition under which paragraphs (d) and (e) apply to a large business is that, in its fiscal year preceding award, it received Department of Defense prime contracts or subcontracts totaling $50 million or more for which certified cost or pricing data were required.
quote: In its fiscal year preceding award of this contract, received Department of Defense (DoD) prime contracts or subcontracts, totaling $50 million or more for which certified cost or pricing data were required

statement: For a large business that, in its fiscal year before award, received DoD prime contracts or subcontracts totaling $10 million or more but less than $50 million for which certified cost or pricing data were required, paragraphs (d) and (e) apply only if the contracting officer has also notified it in writing that they apply.
quote: Was notified, in writing, by the Contracting Officer that paragraphs (d) and (e) of this clause apply

statement: The contractor discloses its estimating system to the administrative contracting officer in writing.
quote: The Contractor shall disclose its estimating system to the Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO), in writing

statement: An estimating system disclosure is acceptable when the documentation both accurately describes the policies, procedures and practices the contractor currently uses in preparing cost proposals and provides sufficient detail for the Government to reasonably make an informed judgment on the acceptability of its estimating practices.
quote: Accurately describes those policies, procedures, and practices that the Contractor currently uses in preparing cost proposals

statement: The contractor must disclose significant changes to its cost estimating system to the administrative contracting officer on a timely basis.
quote: Disclose significant changes to the cost estimating system to the ACO on a timely basis

statement: An acceptable estimating system establishes clear responsibility for preparation, review and approval of cost estimates and budgets.
quote: Establish clear responsibility for preparation, review, and approval of cost estimates and budgets

statement: The system must identify and document the sources of data and the estimating methods and rationale used in developing cost estimates and budgets.
quote: Identify and document the sources of data and the estimating methods and rationale used in developing cost estimates and budgets

statement: The system must provide for internal review of, and accountability for, the acceptability of the estimating system, including the budgetary data supporting indirect cost estimates and comparisons of projected results to actual results.
quote: Provide for internal review of, and accountability for, the acceptability of the estimating system, including the budgetary data supporting indirect cost estimates and comparisons of projected results to actual results

statement: The contractor must respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the contracting officer that identifies material weaknesses in its estimating system.
quote: The Contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the Contracting Officer that identifies material weaknesses in the Contractor's estimating system.

statement: After a final determination of material weaknesses, the contractor must within 45 days of receipt either correct the weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate them.
quote: within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the material weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the material weaknesses

statement: If the contracting officer makes a final determination to disapprove the contractor's estimating system and the contract includes the Contractor Business Systems clause, the contracting officer withholds payments in accordance with that clause.
quote: the Contracting Officer will withhold payments in accordance with that clause

statement: Certified cost or pricing data shall not be obtained for acquisitions at or below the simplified acquisition threshold.
quote: Certified cost or pricing data shall not be obtained for acquisitions at or below the simplified acquisition threshold.

statement: Except in the listed circumstances, the contracting officer shall not require certified cost or pricing data to support any action, including contracts, subcontracts, or modifications.
quote: The contracting officer shall not require certified cost or pricing data to support any action (contracts, subcontracts, or modifications)

statement: The contracting officer shall not require certified cost or pricing data when the contracting officer determines that prices agreed upon are based on adequate price competition.
quote: When the contracting officer determines that prices agreed upon are based on adequate price competition

statement: The contracting officer shall not require certified cost or pricing data when the contracting officer determines that prices agreed upon are based on prices set by law or regulation.
quote: When the contracting officer determines that prices agreed upon are based on prices set by law or regulation

statement: The contracting officer shall not require certified cost or pricing data when a commercial product or commercial service is being acquired.
quote: When a commercial product or commercial serviceis being acquired

statement: The contracting officer shall not require certified cost or pricing data when a waiver has been granted.
quote: When a waiver has been granted (see standards in paragraph (c)(4) of this subsection)

statement: A price is based on adequate price competition when two or more responsible offerors, competing independently, submit priced offers that satisfy the Government's expressed requirement, together with the further conditions stated in the next claim.
quote: Two or more responsible offerors, competing independently, submit priced offers that satisfy the Government's expressed requirement

statement: The head of the contracting activity may, without power of delegation, waive the requirement for submission of certified cost or pricing data in exceptional cases.
quote: The head of the contracting activity (HCA) may, without power of delegation, waive the requirement for submission of certified cost or pricing data in exceptional cases.

statement: Contracting officers must require submission of data other than certified cost or pricing data to the extent necessary to determine a fair and reasonable price.
quote: Contracting officers must require submission of data other than certified cost or pricing data to the extent necessary to determine a fair and reasonable price
note: S-0016 prints the data-other-than-certified provisions under the same section number as the exceptions printed in S-0002.

statement: Where data other than certified cost or pricing data are required, the data must at a minimum include appropriate data on the prices at which the same item or similar items have previously been sold, adequate for determining the reasonableness of the price.
quote: At a minimum, the data must include appropriate data on the prices at which the same item or similar items have previously been sold, adequate for determining the reasonableness of the price.

statement: An offeror who does not comply with a requirement to submit data for a contract or subcontract in accordance with paragraph (a)(1) is ineligible for award, subject to the exception stated in the next claims.
quote: an offeror who does not comply with a requirement to submit data for a contract or subcontract in accordance with paragraph (a)(1) of this subsection is ineligible for award

statement: This subsection prescribes policies for establishing the profit or fee portion of the Government prenegotiation objective in price negotiations based on cost analysis.
quote: This subsection prescribes policies for establishing the profit or fee portion of the Government prenegotiation objective in price negotiations based on cost analysis.

statement: Profit or fee prenegotiation objectives do not necessarily represent net income to contractors; they represent that element of the potential total remuneration that contractors may receive for contract performance over and above allowable costs.
quote: Profit or fee prenegotiation objectives do not necessarily represent net income to contractors. Rather, they represent that element of the potential total remuneration that contractors may receive for contract performance over and above allowable costs.

statement: For experimental, developmental, or research work performed under a cost-plus-fixed-fee contract, the fee shall not exceed 15 percent of the contract's estimated cost, excluding fee.
quote: For experimental, developmental, or research work performed under a cost-plus-fixed-fee contract, the fee shall not exceed 15 percent of the contract's estimated cost, excluding fee.

statement: For architect-engineer services for public works or utilities, the contract price or the estimated cost and fee for production and delivery of designs, plans, drawings, and specifications shall not exceed 6 percent of the estimated cost of construction of the public work or utility, excluding fees.
quote: For architect-engineer services for public works or utilities, the contract price or the estimated cost and fee for production and delivery of designs, plans, drawings, and specifications shall not exceed 6 percent of the estimated cost of construction of the public work or utility, excluding fees.

statement: For other cost-plus-fixed-fee contracts, the fee shall not exceed 10 percent of the contract's estimated cost, excluding fee.
quote: For other cost-plus-fixed-fee contracts, the fee shall not exceed 10 percent of the contract's estimated cost, excluding fee.

statement: When the price negotiation is not based on cost analysis, contracting officers are not required to analyze profit.
quote: When the price negotiation is not based on cost analysis, contracting officers are not required to analyze profit.

statement: Unless clearly inappropriate or not applicable, each common factor outlined in the subsection shall be considered by agencies in developing their structured approaches and by contracting officers in analyzing profit.
quote: Unless it is clearly inappropriate or not applicable, each factor outlined in paragraphs (d)(1)(i) through (vi) of this subsection shall be considered by agencies in developing their structured approaches and by contracting officers in analyzing profit

statement: Subject to the authorities in 1.301(c), agencies making noncompetitive contract awards over $100,000 totaling $50 million or more a year shall use a structured approach for determining the profit or fee objective in those acquisitions that require cost analysis.
quote: agencies making noncompetitive contract awards over $100,000 totaling $50 million or more a year— (i) Shall use a structured approach for determining the profit or fee objective in those acquisitions that require cost analysis

statement: When certified cost or pricing data are required, the contracting officer shall require the contractor to execute a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data using the format in the subsection, and must include the executed certificate in the contract file.
quote: the contracting officer shall require the contractor to execute a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data, using the format in this paragraph, and must include the executed certificate in the contract file

quote: This certification includes the cost or pricing data supporting any advance agreements and forward pricing rate agreements between the offeror and the Government that are part of the proposal.

statement: The certificate applies to the data upon which the contractor's judgment or estimate was based, not to the accuracy of that judgment on future costs or projections.
quote: It applies to the data upon which the judgment or estimate was based.

statement: Possession of a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data is not a substitute for examining and analyzing the contractor's proposal.
quote: Possession of a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data is not a substitute for examining and analyzing the contractor's proposal.

statement: If certified cost or pricing data are requested by the Government and submitted by an offeror but an exception is later found to apply, the data shall not be considered certified cost or pricing data and shall not be certified in accordance with this subsection.
quote: If certified cost or pricing data are requested by the Government and submitted by an offeror, but an exception is later found to apply, the data shall not be considered certified cost or pricing data and shall not be certified in accordance with this subsection.

statement: The certificate states that the submitted cost or pricing data are accurate, complete, and current as of the date inserted in the certificate.
quote: are accurate, complete, and current as of ____**
note: The printed certificate format leaves the as-of date blank for insertion of the date price negotiations were concluded.

statement: The clause applies when a price, including profit or fee, or a reimbursable cost was increased by any significant amount because the contractor or a subcontractor furnished certified cost or pricing data that were not complete, accurate, and current as certified in its Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data.
quote: was increased by any significant amount because— (1) The Contractor or a subcontractor furnished certified cost or pricing data that were not complete, accurate, and current as certified in its Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data

statement: If any price, including profit or fee, or any reimbursable cost was increased by any significant amount because the contractor, a subcontractor or a prospective subcontractor furnished defective certified cost or pricing data, or any of them furnished inaccurate data of any description, the price or cost shall be reduced accordingly and the contract shall be modified to reflect the reduction.
quote: the price or cost shall be reduced accordingly and the contract shall be modified to reflect the reduction.

statement: Any reduction in the contract price under paragraph (a) due to defective data from a prospective subcontractor that was not subsequently awarded the subcontract is limited to the amount, plus applicable overhead and profit markup, described in the next claims.
quote: Any reduction in the contract price under paragraph (a) of this clause due to defective data from a prospective subcontractor that was not subsequently awarded the subcontract shall be limited to the amount, plus applicable overhead and profit markup

statement: If the Contracting Officer determines under paragraph (a) that a price or cost reduction should be made, the Contractor agrees not to raise as a defense the matters listed in the clause, which the next claims quote.
quote: the Contractor agrees not to raise the following matters as a defense

statement: If a price reduction lowers the price of items for which payment was made before the modification, and the contractor or subcontractor knowingly submitted certified cost or pricing data that were incomplete, inaccurate, or noncurrent, the contractor is liable for a penalty equal to the amount of the overpayment, payable when the overpayment is repaid.
quote: A penalty equal to the amount of the overpayment, if the Contractor or subcontractor knowingly submitted certified cost or pricing data that were incomplete, inaccurate, or noncurrent.

statement: When a reduction reduces the price of items already paid, the contractor is liable for interest compounded daily on the amount of the overpayment.
quote: Interest compounded daily, as required by 26 U.S.C. 6622, on the amount of such overpayment

statement: A contracting officer should request field pricing assistance when the information available at the buying activity is inadequate to determine a fair and reasonable price.
quote: The contracting officer should request field pricing assistance when the information available at the buying activity is inadequate to determine a fair and reasonable price.

statement: A field pricing request must be tailored to reflect the minimum essential supplementary information needed to conduct a technical or cost or pricing analysis.
quote: The contracting officer shall tailor requests to reflect the minimum essential supplementary information needed to conduct a technical or cost or pricing analysis.

statement: The type of information and level of detail requested must be tailored in accordance with the specialized resources available at the buying activity and the magnitude and complexity of the required analysis.
quote: The contracting officer shall tailor the type of information and level of detail requested in accordance with the specialized resources available at the buying activity and the magnitude and complexity of the required analysis.

statement: Field pricing assistance is generally available to provide technical, audit, and special reports associated with the cost elements of a proposal, including subcontracts.
quote: Field pricing assistance is generally available to provide— (i) Technical, audit, and special reports associated with the cost elements of a proposal, including subcontracts;

statement: Field pricing information and other reports may include proprietary or source selection information, which must be appropriately identified and protected.
quote: Field pricing information and other reports may include proprietary or source selection information (see 2.101). This information must be appropriately identified and protected accordingly.

statement: Audit and field pricing information, whether written or reported telephonically or electronically, must be made a part of the official contract file.
quote: Audit and field pricing information, whether written or reported telephonically or electronically, shall be made a part of the official contract file

statement: The auditor must not reveal audit conclusions or recommendations to the offeror or contractor without obtaining the contracting officer's concurrence, but the auditor may discuss statements of facts with the contractor.
quote: The auditor shall not reveal the audit conclusions or recommendations to the offeror/contractor without obtaining the concurrence of the contracting officer. However, the auditor may discuss statements of facts with the contractor.

statement: The contracting officer must not request a separate preaward audit of indirect costs unless the information already available from an existing audit, completed within the preceding 12 months, is considered inadequate for determining the reasonableness of the proposed indirect costs.
quote: The contracting officer shall not request a separate preaward audit of indirect costs unless the information already available from an existing audit, completed within the preceding 12 months, is considered inadequate for determining the reasonableness of the proposed indirect costs

statement: The administrative contracting officer or the auditor, as appropriate, must notify the contracting officer immediately if the data provided for review is so deficient as to preclude review or audit.
quote: The ACO or the auditor, as appropriate, shall notify the contracting officer immediately if the data provided for review is so deficient as to preclude review or audit

statement: If the offeror or contractor again refuses to provide adequate data or access to necessary data, the contracting officer shall withhold the award or price adjustment and refer the contract action to a higher authority.
quote: Should the offeror/contractor again refuse to provide adequate data, or provide access to necessary data, the contracting officer shall withhold the award or price adjustment and refer the contract action to a higher authority

statement: When field pricing assistance is requested, contracting officers are encouraged to team with appropriate field experts throughout the acquisition process, including negotiations.
quote: When field pricing assistance is requested, contracting officers are encouraged to team with appropriate field experts throughout the acquisition process, including negotiations

statement: Identifying general market conditions affecting determinations of commerciality and a fair and reasonable price is one item in the list of information that helps contracting officers make those determinations, in the list of what field pricing assistance can provide under FAR 15.404-2(a)(2)(iii).
quote: Identifying general market conditions affecting determinations of commerciality and a fair and reasonable price

statement: The contracting officer is responsible for the determination of a fair and reasonable price for the prime contract, including subcontracting costs.
quote: The contracting officer is responsible for the determination of a fair and reasonable price for the prime contract, including subcontracting costs.

statement: The contracting officer should consider whether a contractor or subcontractor has an approved purchasing system, has performed cost or price analysis of proposed subcontractor prices, or has negotiated the subcontract prices before negotiation of the prime contract.
quote: The contracting officer should consider whether a contractor or subcontractor has an approved purchasing system, has performed cost or price analysis of proposed subcontractor prices, or has negotiated the subcontract prices before negotiation of the prime contract

statement: Those considerations do not relieve the contracting officer from the responsibility to analyze the contractor's submission, including subcontractor's certified cost or pricing data.
quote: This does not relieve the contracting officer from the responsibility to analyze the contractor's submission, including subcontractor's certified cost or pricing data.

statement: The prime contractor or a subcontractor shall conduct appropriate cost or price analyses to establish the reasonableness of proposed subcontract prices.
quote: The prime contractor or subcontractor shall— (1) Conduct appropriate cost or price analyses to establish the reasonableness of proposed subcontract prices;

statement: The results of those analyses must be included in the price proposal.
quote: The prime contractor or subcontractor shall— (1) Conduct appropriate cost or price analyses to establish the reasonableness of proposed subcontract prices; (2) Include the results of these analyses in the price proposal;

statement: A contractor or subcontractor that is required to submit certified cost or pricing data must also obtain and analyze certified cost or pricing data before awarding any subcontract, purchase order, or modification expected to exceed the certified cost or pricing data threshold.
quote: Any contractor or subcontractor that is required to submit certified cost or pricing data also shall obtain and analyze certified cost or pricing data before awarding any subcontract, purchase order, or modification expected to exceed the certified cost or pricing data threshold

statement: The subcontracts for which certified cost or pricing data is to be submitted to the Government are those that are the lower of either $20 million or more, or both more than the pertinent certified cost or pricing data threshold and more than 10 percent of the prime contractor's proposed price, unless the contracting officer believes such submission is unnecessary.
quote: the lower of either— (i) $20 million or more; or (ii) Both more than the pertinent certified cost or pricing data threshold and more than 10 percent of the prime contractor's proposed price, unless the contracting officer believes such submission is unnecessary.

statement: The contracting officer should require the contractor or subcontractor to submit to the Government, or cause the submission of, subcontractor certified cost or pricing data below the thresholds in paragraph (c)(1).
quote: The contracting officer should require the contractor or subcontractor to submit to the Government (or cause submission of) subcontractor certified cost or pricing data below the thresholds in paragraph (c)(1) of this subsection

quote: Subcontractor certified cost or pricing data shall be current, accurate, and complete as of the date of price agreement, or, if applicable, an earlier date agreed upon by the parties and specified on the contractor's Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data

statement: If there is more than one prospective subcontractor for any given work, the contractor need only submit certified cost or pricing data for the prospective subcontractor most likely to receive the award.
quote: If there is more than one prospective subcontractor for any given work, the contractor need only submit to the Government certified cost or pricing data for the prospective subcontractor most likely to receive the award.

statement: Should-cost reviews differ from traditional evaluation methods because they do not assume that a contractor's historical costs reflect efficient and economical operation.
quote: Should-cost reviews differ from traditional evaluation methods because they do not assume that a contractor's historical costs reflect efficient and economical operation.

statement: Should-cost reviews evaluate the economy and efficiency of the contractor's existing work force, methods, materials, equipment, real property, operating systems, and management.
quote: these reviews evaluate the economy and efficiency of the contractor's existing work force, methods, materials, equipment, real property, operating systems, and management

statement: These reviews are accomplished by a multi-functional team of Government contracting, contract administration, pricing, audit, and engineering representatives.
quote: These reviews are accomplished by a multi-functional team of Government contracting, contract administration, pricing, audit, and engineering representatives.

statement: There are two types of should-cost reviews, program should-cost review and overhead should-cost review, and these reviews may be performed together or independently.
quote: There are two types of should-cost reviews—program should-cost review (see paragraph (b) of this subsection) and overhead should-cost review (see paragraph (c) of this subsection). These should-cost reviews may be performed together or independently.

statement: When a program should-cost review is conducted relative to a contractor proposal, a separate audit report on the proposal is required.
quote: When a program should-cost review is conducted relative to a contractor proposal, a separate audit report on the proposal is required.

statement: An overhead should-cost review is used to evaluate indirect costs such as fringe benefits, shipping and receiving, real property and equipment, depreciation, plant maintenance and security, taxes, and general and administrative activities.
quote: An overhead should-cost review is used to evaluate indirect costs, such as fringe benefits, shipping and receiving, real property, and equipment, depreciation, plant maintenance and security, taxes, and general and administrative activities.

statement: The contracting officer shall establish a follow-up plan to monitor the correction of the uneconomical or inefficient practices.
quote: The contracting officer shall establish a follow-up plan to monitor the correction of the uneconomical or inefficient practices.

statement: When a program should-cost review is planned, the contracting officer should state this fact in the acquisition plan or acquisition plan updates and in the solicitation.
quote: When a program should-cost review is planned, the contracting officer should state this fact in the acquisition plan or acquisition plan updates (see subpart 7.1) and in the solicitation.

quote: As soon as practicable after agreement on price, but before contract award (except for unpriced actions such as letter contracts), the Offeror shall submit a Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data

quote: The Offeror is responsible for determining whether a subcontractor qualifies for an exception from the requirement for submission of certified cost or pricing data on the basis of adequate price competition

quote: No cost data may be required from a prospective subcontractor in any case in which there are sufficient non-Government sales of the same item to establish reasonableness of price.

quote: For a commercial product or commercial service exception, the Offeror shall submit, at a minimum, information that is adequate for determining commerciality and evaluating the reasonableness of the price for this acquisition

quote: , and either the actual subcontract price or the actual cost to the contractor, if not subcontracted, provided the data on which the actual subcontract price is based are not themselves defective.

quote: Establish and maintain procedures to timely notify the Contracting Officer, in writing, if— (i) The Contractor changes the amount of subcontract effort after award such that it exceeds 70 percent of the total cost of the work to be performed under the contract, task order, or delivery order.

statement: That notification must identify the revised cost of the subcontract effort and include verification that the contractor will provide added value.

statement: The contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the contracting officer that identifies material weaknesses in its purchasing system.
quote: The Contractor shall respond within 30 days to a written initial determination from the Contracting Officer that identifies material weaknesses in the Contractor's purchasing system

statement: After the contracting officer's final determination of material weaknesses, the contractor has 45 days from receipt either to correct the material weaknesses or to submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate them.
quote: within 45 days of receipt of the final determination, either correct the material weaknesses or submit an acceptable corrective action plan showing milestones and actions to eliminate the weaknesses

statement: If the contracting officer makes a final determination to disapprove the purchasing system and the contract includes the Contractor Business Systems clause, payments are withheld in accordance with that clause.
quote: If the Contracting Officer makes a final determination to disapprove the Contractor's purchasing system, and the contract includes the clause at 252.242-7005, Contractor Business Systems, the Contracting Officer will withhold payments in accordance with that clause

statement: Under Alternate I, paragraphs (a) through (f) of the clause do not apply unless the contractor is subject to the Cost Accounting Standards under 41 U.S.C. chapter 15, as implemented at 48 CFR 9903.201-1.

note: Alternate I deletes paragraphs (c)(1) through (c)(18) and (c)(22) through (c)(24) and renumbers paragraphs (c)(19) through (c)(21) of the basic clause.

statement: An acceptable purchasing system is one that complies with the system criteria in paragraph (c) of the clause.
quote: Acceptable purchasing system means a purchasing system that complies with the system criteria in paragraph (c) of this clause

statement: The prime contractor is responsible for managing contract performance, including planning, placing, and administering subcontracts as necessary to ensure the lowest overall cost and technical risk to the Government.
quote: The prime contractor is responsible for managing contract performance, including planning, placing, and administering subcontracts as necessary to ensure the lowest overall cost and technical risk to the Government.

statement: When make-or-buy programs are required, the Government may reserve the right to review and agree on the contractor's program when necessary to ensure negotiation of reasonable contract prices, satisfactory performance, or implementation of socioeconomic policies.

statement: Consent to subcontracts and review of contractors' purchasing systems are separate actions covered in part 44.
quote: Consent to subcontracts and review of contractors' purchasing systems are separate actions covered in part 44.

statement: As used in FAR 15.407-2, a make item means an item or work effort to be produced or performed by the prime contractor or its affiliates, subsidiaries, or divisions.
quote: Make item, as used in this subsection, means an item or work effort to be produced or performed by the prime contractor or its affiliates, subsidiaries, or divisions

statement: Contracting officers may require prospective contractors to submit make-or-buy program plans for negotiated acquisitions requiring certified cost or pricing data whose estimated value is $20 million or more; an exception for research and development is stated in the claim that follows.
quote: Contracting officers may require prospective contractors to submit make-or-buy program plans for negotiated acquisitions requiring certified cost or pricing data whose estimated value is $20 million or more

statement: That authority does not apply when the proposed contract is for research or development and, if prototypes or hardware are involved, no significant follow-on production is anticipated.
quote: except when the proposed contract is for research or development and, if prototypes or hardware are involved, no significant follow-on production is anticipated

statement: For negotiated acquisitions whose estimated value is under $20 million, a make-or-buy program may be required only if the contracting officer determines that the information is necessary and documents the reasons in the contract file.
quote: for negotiated acquisitions whose estimated value is under $20 million only if the contracting officer— (i) Determines that the information is necessary; and (ii) Documents the reasons in the contract file

statement: When prospective contractors must submit proposed make-or-buy programs, the solicitation shall include a statement that the program and required supporting information must accompany the offer.

statement: The information required from a contractor in a make-or-buy program is confined to those major items or work efforts that normally would require company management review of the make-or-buy decision because they are complex, costly, needed in large quantities, or require additional equipment or real property to produce.
quote: confined to those major items or work efforts that normally would require company management review of the make-or-buy decision because they are complex, costly, needed in large quantities, or require additional equipment or real property to produce.

statement: Raw materials, commercial products, commercial services, and off-the-shelf items shall not be included in a make-or-buy program unless their potential impact on contract cost or schedule is critical.
quote: Raw materials, commercial products, commercial services (see 2.101), and off-the-shelf items (see 46.101) shall not be included, unless their potential impact on contract cost or schedule is critical.

statement: Normally, make-or-buy programs should not include items or work efforts estimated to cost less than 1 percent of the total estimated contract price or any minimum dollar amount set by the agency.
quote: Normally, make-or-buy programs should not include items or work efforts estimated to cost less than 1 percent of the total estimated contract price or any minimum dollar amount set by the agency.

statement: The list of information that the offeror's make-or-buy program should include or be supported by includes identification of proposed subcontractors, if known, and their location and size status.
quote: Identification of proposed subcontractors, if known, and their location and size status

statement: Contracting officers shall evaluate and negotiate proposed make-or-buy programs as soon as practicable after their receipt and before contract award.
quote: Contracting officers shall evaluate and negotiate proposed make-or-buy programs as soon as practicable after their receipt and before contract award.

statement: If the contractor proposes to reverse the categorization of such items during contract performance, the contract price shall be subject to equitable reduction; the items are those the contracting officer agreed to accept as make items and specified in the contract under paragraph (f)(2).
quote: If the contractor proposes to reverse the categorization of such items during contract performance, the contract price shall be subject to equitable reduction.

statement: The contracting officer may incorporate the make-or-buy program in negotiated contracts for major systems or their subsystems or components, regardless of contract type.
quote: The contracting officer may incorporate the make-or-buy program in negotiated contracts for— (1) Major systems (see part 34) or their subsystems or components, regardless of contract type;

statement: For other supplies and services, one of two conditions for incorporating the make-or-buy program is that the contract is a cost-reimbursable contract, or a cost-sharing contract in which the contractor's share of the cost is less than 25 percent.
quote: Other supplies and services if— (i) The contract is a cost-reimbursable contract, or a cost-sharing contract in which the contractor's share of the cost is less than 25 percent; and

statement: For other supplies and services, incorporation also requires, in addition to the cost-type condition, that the contracting officer determines that technical or cost risks justify Government review and approval of changes or additions to the make-or-buy program.
quote: and (ii) The contracting officer determines that technical or cost risks justify Government review and approval of changes or additions to the make-or-buy program

statement: When the make-or-buy program is to be incorporated in the contract and the design status of the product does not permit accurate precontract identification of major items or work efforts, the contracting officer shall notify the prospective contractor in writing.
quote: When the program is to be incorporated in the contract and the design status of the product being acquired does not permit accurate precontract identification of major items or work efforts, the contracting officer shall notify the prospective contractor in writing

statement: An offeror's make-or-buy program should include or be supported by the information listed in FAR 15.407-2(e)(2).

statement: In a fixed-price incentive or cost-plus-incentive-fee contract in which the contracting officer agrees to proposed make items despite their availability from another firm at lower prices, the contracting officer shall specify these items in the contract and state that they are subject to paragraph (d) of the clause at 52.215-9, Changes or Additions to Make-or-Buy Program.
quote: If this situation occurs in any fixed-price incentive or cost-plus-incentive-fee contract, the contracting officer shall specify these items in the contract and state that they are subject to paragraph (d) of the clause at 52.215-9, Changes or Additions to Make-or-Buy Program (see 15.408(a)).

statement: A contracting officer who would normally not agree to proposed make items because another firm offers the products or services at lower prices may nonetheless agree if an overall lower Governmentwide cost would result or it is otherwise in the best interest of the Government.
quote: However, the contracting officer may agree to these as “make items” if an overall lower Governmentwide cost would result or it is otherwise in the best interest of the Government.

statement: The written notice tells the prospective contractor that the items or efforts, when identifiable, shall be added under the clause at 52.215-9, Changes or Additions to Make-or-Buy Program.
quote: the contracting officer shall notify the prospective contractor in writing that these items or efforts, when identifiable, shall be added under the clause at 52.215-9, Changes or Additions to Make-or-Buy Program.

statement: The contracting officer evaluates the contractor's response and notifies the contractor in writing of the final determination concerning remaining material weaknesses and the adequacy of any proposed or completed corrective action.
quote: The Contracting Officer will evaluate the Contractor's response and notify the Contractor, in writing, of the Contracting Officer's final determination concerning— (i) Remaining material weaknesses; (ii) The adequacy of any proposed or completed corrective action;

statement: The final determination also concerns system disapproval, if the contracting officer determines that one or more material weaknesses remain.
quote: (iii) System disapproval, if the Contracting Officer determines that one or more material weaknesses remain.

statement: If the contractor disagrees with the initial determination, the contractor shall state, in writing, its rationale for disagreeing.
quote: If the Contractor disagrees with the initial determination, the Contractor shall state, in writing, its rationale for disagreeing.
